newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Milosevic sworn in as Yugoslav president.
newsitem.headline: Milosevic sworn in as Yugoslav president.

text.p: Slobodan Milosevic was sworn in as Yugoslav president in the federal parliament on Wednesday, completing the switch from president of Serbia, dominant partner in the two-member federation.

"I swear that I will carry out my duties conscientiously and responsibly, according to the Constitution and the law and that I will fight to safeguard the sovereignty, independence and integrity of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia," he said, taking the oath of office.
Milosevic was elected president of Yugoslavia by the federal parliament on July 15 in keeping with the federal constitution.
He wanted to be elected by general ballot but the move was opposed by tiny Montenegro which feared amendments to the constitution this would involve would infringe its rights in the federation.
After the violent breakup of the old six-member Yugoslav federation in the early 1990s, Yugoslavia now comprises only Serbia and Montenegro.
Milosevic resigned as Serbian president earlier in the day. The post will be administered by the speaker of the Serbian parliament, Dragan Tomic, until presidential elections due within 60 days.
